target.title: feat(web): restore the last project location

scenario.action: Opened a registered project Git route with query and fragment and waited for the persistence debounce.
scenario.expected: The exact project, pathname, query, and fragment are stored in workspace UI state.
scenario.observed: The browser stayed at /p/cezar/git?qa=restore#changed and GET /api/v1/workspace/ui-state returned the same four location fields.

scenario.action: Cold-navigated the same browser session to the exact bare root and waited for startup queries.
scenario.expected: Bare root is replaced with the saved project route, including query and fragment, and Back does not return to a transient root entry.
scenario.observed: The URL became /p/cezar/git?qa=restore#changed; Back remained on that restored URL.

scenario.action: Opened an explicit project Settings deep link, visited global Settings, then reopened the bare root at a 390 x 844 viewport.
scenario.expected: The explicit project URL remains authoritative, global Settings does not overwrite it, and bare-root restoration remains usable on a narrow viewport.
scenario.observed: Workspace state retained /p/cezar/settings/agents?manual=1#config while global Settings was open; bare root restored that exact URL and rendered the Agents settings surface without browser errors.

scenario.action: Seeded a structurally valid saved route for a project absent from the registry and opened the exact bare root.
scenario.expected: The stale saved route is ignored and startup falls back to the boot project's Tasks page.
scenario.observed: The URL became /p/42766454-3ead-4ea4-8f05-aab273e5cf8b/ and the boot-project empty Tasks page rendered without browser errors.

notes: The browser console and page-error collection were empty at the restored mobile route and at the missing-project fallback.
The repository test environment uses CEZ_DRY_RUN=1 and an isolated CEZ_HOME under .ai/qa; no real agent login or developer workspace state was used.
This change does not add a committed browser-level test; the PR has extensive unit/component coverage and this run supplies real-browser evidence.
